newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong moves to curb property speculation.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong moves to curb property speculation.

text.p: The Hong Kong government on Wednesday welcomed voluntary moves by developers to curb rampant property speculation, but warned it would impose tougher measures if they proved insufficient.

"If voluntary compliance with these measures by developers does not achieve the desired objectives, we will not hesitate to take action to introduce appropriate measures to restore the proper operation of the market," Housing Secretary Dominic Wong said.
He told the territory's legislature that local developers would immediately adopt measures aimed at dampening speculation.
"We welcome the introduction of new sales arrangements announced by the Real Estate Developers' Association of Hong Kong (REDA) ... as a first step to dampen speculation through companies," he said.
The measures will bar companies that buy uncompleted flats from changing company directorships before the signing of sales and purchase agreements.
Until now speculators have used shell companies to buy flats. They then sell the company and change the directorship to get around restrictions on the rapid resale of flats.
Companies will also be limited to buying the last 15 percent of each batch of flats, leaving the rest to individuals.
Developers further promised to clearly state in sales brochures and newspaper advertisements the total number of flats available for pre-sale in each housing development.
Finally, they undertook to ensure that the 10 percent of flats allowed for internal sales to persons connected to the developer would only go to genuine end-users.
"Taken together, they will help to protect the interests of genuine flat buyers and greatly dampen speculation in the residential property market," Wong said.
Consumers, legislators and business lobbies have all voiced concerns over a rise of 20 to 30 percent in residential property prices in 1996, putting pressure on the government to act.

The focus of concern is the luxury sector, where the government says speculation is rampant. Prices in this sector jumped 30 to 40 percent last year, with much of the rise coming in the fourth quarter.
Speculators have reportedly paid up to HK$2 million (US$258,000) at recent luxury flat sales merely for the right to be first in line. ($1 = HK$7.74)
